text:
nora: Heads-up — onboarding sample using Next.js Edge runtime failed in customer sandbox. Error: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when Next's esbuild step tries to bundle the SDK. Repro below.

between: can you paste the import line + package.json?

nora: import in app/edge/route.js:
```js
import { create } from 'redwood-inference';
export const runtime = 'edge';
const c = create({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await c.generate('hi');
```
error from build: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './dist/browser/index.js' is not defined by "exports"`
package.json snippet shipped in SDK v4.0.0:
```json
{"name":"redwood-inference","version":"4.0.0","main":"dist/index.cjs","exports":{"./dist/browser/index.js":"./dist/index.cjs"},"types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```

ben: interesting — bundlers often try to resolve a browser/esm-ish entry (esbuild/next will prefer an ESM/browser subpath). Here the exports map only exposes a CJS file under that browser path, so resolution fails. Next's optimizer runs on the server and is stricter about package exports.

rasheed: also saw TS problems in monorepo samples: editors show no declarations for the package when the exports map is incomplete. When "exports" exists, TS will not always fallback to top-level "types".

ivy: quick local test: changing exports to include a root entry with import/require and a types subpath fixed both the Next build and editor resolution. Example used in my repro:
```json
{"exports":{
  ".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "types":"./dist/index.d.ts"},
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},"types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
This allowed Next/esbuild to prefer the ESM browser build and TypeScript to resolve declarations.

ben: alternative pattern if producing a full ESM build is heavy: ship a tiny ESM wrapper at dist/esm/index.mjs that re-exports the same API via dynamic import from CJS or re-implements a small bootstrap. That keeps bundle size small but satisfies bundler resolution.

rasheed: note for docs: a lot of bundlers check for a browser/exports/ import condition. If you only expose a CJS subpath, you can break bundlers and edge runtimes. We should document the safe export map pattern and example for Next/Vercel/Cloudflare + TS.

nora: immediate actions I propose:
- revert the change that added the restrictive mapping (cut patch 4.0.1) (P0)
- publish a follow-up that adds proper dual exports + types + package.json subpath (P0)
- add a small CI job that runs Next's optimizer against our sample app and a cloudflare pages preview on packaging PRs (P1)

pkg-bot: PR opened: revert/export-fix (#3402) — CI started (unit + node matrix).

ivy: short-term workaround for customers: import the explicit ESM path (`import { create } from 'redwood-inference/dist/esm/index.mjs'`) or pin to 3.x until patch lands. Also mention adding a resolutions override in monorepos if they use yarn/PNPM.

ben: agree on CI matrix. We missed this because existing packaging tests only ran node-based smoke tests and not bundler/next optimizer. I'll add next/webpack/esbuild smoke jobs for packaging PRs.

nora: thanks folks. I'll attach failing customer logs to the issue and coordinate the patch. Will also add a short KB note for support with the workaround. :thumbsup:
